transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I need help dealing with the people who are constantly monitoring me. A local organization has been tracking my movements and tapping my phone, and I know they are trying to sabotage my life. I just need someone to help me make them stop.
Have you been feeling unusually high-spirited or energetic, or conversely, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness or a lack of energy during this time?
No, I haven't really felt unusually energetic or persistently sad. My mood has been relatively normal, aside from just being stressed about the people monitoring me.
Beyond these concerns about being monitored, have you noticed any changes in your ability to take care of daily tasks, your interest in hobbies, or your desire to interact with others?

My daily life, hobbies, and work are actually completely fine, and I manage all my responsibilities normally. The only difference is that I have to take extra precautions now, like changing my route home to avoid being followed. Other than that, my routine and social life haven't really changed.

latest_inference.note: The patient exhibits a fixed, non-bizarre belief regarding being monitored and sabotaged, while explicitly denying mood symptoms (ruling out schizoaffective or bipolar disorders) and maintaining functional stability in daily life and work. The lack of functional impairment or other prominent symptoms of schizophrenia (such as disorganized speech or negative symptoms) makes Delusional Disorder the most accurate diagnosis.
